issue_request: FHIR-7080 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core technical correction for lifecycle.html section 1.12.4. It reported a copy/paste error where the Entity Availability paragraph said the characteristic states were for the clinical workflow process pattern, and asked that the wording refer to the entity availability pattern instead.
initial_application: The Jira comment says the issue was fixed as part of FHIR-7079. FHIR-7079 records SVN revision 6428, mirrored in git as 87d26ec5a6985bd9bc7ebc45b2ccbdca3c2e5f02, which changed the Entity Availability paragraph from clinical-workflow wording to entity-availability wording while also correcting the adjacent Request/Order copy/paste text.
additional_context: source/lifecycle.html is an active built narrative page because publish.ini lists lifecycle.html and source/hierarchy.xml includes it as Resource Life Cycles. Later lifecycle terminology work, including FHIR-7363 and the existing combined-branch commit 10d3d9f72d992bba52cab60c35fe82e7b7de3f44, standardized this page on life cycle rather than pattern terminology without reversing the FHIR-7080 correction. Exact-key and lifecycle-focused Zulip and Confluence searches found no community record that changes the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current Entity Availability Life Cycle section already says that the characteristic states are for the entity availability life cycle, so the reported copy/paste error is not present in the current built source.
